banner.startingSub: Almost there. On the first start the server downloads the game files, which takes a moment.
banner.stoppedSub: Your world is saved. Start it whenever you want to play.

setup.title: Welcome to MorniHosting
setup.subtitle: Three short steps and your panel is ready.
setup.languageHint: You can change it any time in your account.
setup.accountHint: This account manages everything. There is no default password, only the one you choose here.
setup.usernameHint: 3 to 32 characters: letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore
setup.passwordHint: At least 10 characters. A sentence of several words is strong and easy to remember.
setup.doneText: Your panel is ready. Next, create your first server; it takes less than a minute.
setup.dockerWarning: Docker is not reachable right now. You can continue, but servers only start once Docker runs.

login.title: Sign in
login.subtitle: Sign in to manage your servers.
login.twoFactorText: Open your authenticator app and enter the 6-digit code for MorniHosting.

dashboard.title: Your servers
dashboard.subtitle: {{running}} of {{total}} servers running · {{players}}
dashboard.emptyText: Create your first Minecraft server. You pick the game version and size, we take care of the rest.
dashboard.emptyImport: Already have a server? Import it as a ZIP.
dashboard.noAccess: No server has been shared with you yet. Ask your administrator for access.

card.moddedHint: Modpacks often need 2 to 3 minutes on their first start.

server.noPermission: You do not have the rights for this on this server.

connection.title: Connection
connection.reachableText: Friends can connect from anywhere. Checked {{time}}.
connection.unreachableText: It works at home but not from outside yet. Usually a port forward is missing: forward {{protocol}} port {{port}} to {{lanIp}} in your router.
connection.unknownText: Check whether friends can reach you from the internet.
connection.notRunning: Start the server to check reachability.
connection.portForwardSteps:
1. Open your router's web interface (often 192.168.0.1 or 192.168.1.1).
2. Look for “Port forwarding”.
3. Add a rule for this device: {{protocol}}, port {{port}}, target {{lanIp}}.
4. Save and click “Check again” here.
connection.playitText: No access to the router? playit.gg makes your server reachable without port forwarding.
connection.netbirdError: NetBird could not set up the address: {{reason}}
connection.atHome: You are on the same home network right now – join from here with this address:
connection.bedrockNoSrv: Bedrock knows no addresses with a built-in port: in the game, put the address above into “Server address” and {{port}} into “Port”. Only a server on {{standard}} works without a port.

stats.noData: No measurements yet. They appear once the server runs.
stats.title: History

console.title: Console
console.placeholder: Type a command, e.g. say hello
console.notRunning: The server is off. Start it to send commands.
console.noPermission: You may not view this server's console.
console.noCommandPermission: You may read the console but not send commands.
console.history: Use ↑ and ↓ for earlier commands, Tab to complete.
console.commandFailed: The command did not reach the server.

out-of-memory.title: Not enough memory
out-of-memory.text: The server had {{memoryMb}} MB and needed more. This often happens with modpacks or many players.
out-of-memory.fix: Give the server more memory (e.g. 2 GB more) and restart it.

wrong-java.title: Wrong Java version
wrong-java.text: Part of the server needs Java {{java}}, but a different version was started.
wrong-java.fix: Set the Java version to “Automatic” or Java {{java}} in the settings.

missing-dependency.title: A required plugin or mod is missing
missing-dependency.fix: Install {{dependency}} from the marketplace or remove {{plugin}}.

port-in-use.title: The port is already in use
port-in-use.text: Another program or server already uses this port.
port-in-use.fix: Pick a free port in the settings (e.g. 25566) and restart.

eula.title: Minecraft EULA not accepted
eula.text: The server does not start without agreeing to the EULA.
eula.fix: Start the server again; MorniHosting sets the agreement automatically.

version-not-found.title: This version does not exist
version-not-found.text: The selected game version could not be downloaded.
version-not-found.fix: Pick a different version in the settings.

mod-version-mismatch.title: Mods do not match the game version
mod-version-mismatch.text: At least one mod was built for a different Minecraft version.
mod-version-mismatch.fix: Check the mods for updates in the marketplace or remove the mismatching mod.

world-broken.title: The world cannot be loaded
world-broken.text: The world files seem to be damaged.
world-broken.fix: Restore a backup. Under “Backups” that takes one click.

plugin-error.title: A plugin is causing trouble
plugin-error.fix: Update {{plugin}} or switch it off under “Plugins” for now.

start-failed.title: The server could not start
start-failed.fix: Check that Docker is running and try again.

unknown.title: Unknown cause
unknown.text: The server stopped unexpectedly (code {{exitCode}}). The last lines below usually give a hint.
unknown.fix: Restart the server. If it happens again, take a close look at the console.

download-failed.title: Game files could not be downloaded
download-failed.text: On its first start the server downloads the game files from the internet. That failed.
download-failed.fix: Check the server's internet connection (DNS, firewall) and start it again.

create.title: New server
create.subtitle: A few steps to your own Minecraft server.
create.editionTitle: Which devices do you play on?
create.javaText: For PC and Mac. Plugins and mods possible.
create.bedrockText: For phones, tablets, consoles and the Windows Store version.

software.paper: Fast and stable, with plugins. The best choice for most.
software.purpur: Like Paper, with many extra settings.
software.vanilla: The original by Mojang, without plugins.
software.fabric: Lightweight for mods such as Sodium or Create.
software.forge: The classic for big mods and modpacks.
software.velocity: A proxy that links several servers into one network.

create.versionHint: Pick the version your friends play.
create.versionsFailed: The version list could not be loaded.
create.sizeHint: We recommend {{recommended}}. More helps with many players and mods.
create.ramFree: About {{free}} is free on the host right now.
create.ramWarn: That is more than the host has free right now.
create.nameTitle: What should your server be called?
create.name: Name
create.portHint: Default is {{port}}. Every server needs its own port.

import.title: Import server
import.subtitle: Upload your existing server folder as a ZIP. World, plugins and settings are kept.
import.drop: Drop the ZIP file here or click
import.dropHint: Up to {{size}}. The folder contents (server.properties, world …) can sit directly in the ZIP or in one subfolder.

playersTab.proxy: A proxy has no player list of its own. Manage players on the servers behind it.
playersTab.offline: The server is off. You can still edit operators, the whitelist and bans; changes apply on the next start.
playersTab.offlineBedrock: The server is off. You can still edit the allowlist; everything else needs the server running.
playersTab.onlineText: Who is playing right now. Kicking only disconnects; banning keeps them from coming back.
playersTab.opsText: Operators may use every command in the game, e.g. /gamemode or /tp. Only give this to people you trust.
playersTab.opsTextBedrock: Operators may use commands in the game. On Bedrock, give this in the game or the console.
playersTab.whitelistText: When it is on, only players on this list can join. Handy for a private server with friends.
playersTab.bannedText: Banned players can't join until you lift the ban.

confirm.kickText: They are disconnected and can join again right away.
confirm.banText: They are disconnected and can't join until you lift the ban.

playersTab.title: Players
playersTab.intro: Who is online, who is OP and who may join through the whitelist. Kick, ban or OP with one click.

general.title: General
general.text: Name, size and version of your server. Changes apply on the next start.
general.memoryHint: Recommended: {{recommended}}. Too little RAM makes the server lag or crash.
general.javaHint: Minecraft needs a matching Java version. Automatic picks {{auto}}.
general.downgrade: You picked an older version. That can damage your world. Make a backup first.
general.domainHint: Optional. Shown instead of the IP, e.g. mc.myname.com.
general.autoStartHint: Starts the server when the machine or the panel restarts.
general.publicPortHint: When NetBird, playit.gg or your router use a different port to the outside. The address card then shows that one.

properties.title: Game settings
properties.text: The most important settings from server.properties, explained in plain words.
properties.range: Please enter a number from {{min}} to {{max}}.
properties.managedText: The panel sets these itself so the port and the console keep working.

worlds.title: Worlds
worlds.text: All worlds of your server. The active world is the one being played.
worlds.activateHint: Play this world on the next start
worlds.none: No world yet. It is created on the first start.
worlds.resetHint: The active world goes to the trash; a new one is created on the next start.
worlds.resetText: The active world (with Nether and End) stays in the trash for 7 days. Minecraft creates a new world on the next start.
worlds.resetDone: The old world is in the trash. Start the server for the new world.
worlds.seedHint: Optional. Same seed = same world. Leave empty for a random world.

icon.title: Server picture
icon.text: The picture next to your server in the server list. Any picture works; we crop it to 64 × 64 pixels.

danger.text: Removes the server with all its settings, schedules and backups from the panel.
danger.confirmArchive: The server disappears from the panel. Its files stay in the archive folder on the host.
danger.confirmFiles: The server and all its files, worlds and backups are deleted for good.
danger.deleteFiles: Also delete all files and worlds
danger.deleteFilesHint: If unticked, they are moved to the panel's archive folder.

settings.intro: Adjust how the server starts. Changes apply after the next restart.

motd.label: Description (MOTD)
motd.hint: The text below the server name in the server list. Two lines, with colours.

server-name.label: Server name
server-name.hint: What Bedrock players see in their server list.

difficulty.label: Difficulty
difficulty.hint: How dangerous monsters are and how fast hunger drains.

hardcore.label: Hardcore
hardcore.hint: Players who die become spectators and can't keep playing.

pvp.label: Player vs player (PvP)
pvp.hint: Whether players can hurt each other.

force-gamemode.label: Force game mode
force-gamemode.hint: Always resets players to the default game mode when they join.

allow-cheats.label: Allow cheats
allow-cheats.hint: Allows commands such as /give or /time in the game.

max-players.label: Maximum players
max-players.hint: How many players can be online at the same time.

white-list.label: Whitelist
white-list.hint: Only players on the whitelist can join (see the Players tab).

enforce-whitelist.label: Enforce whitelist right away
enforce-whitelist.hint: Kicks players who are not (or no longer) on the whitelist immediately.

allow-list.label: Allowlist
allow-list.hint: Only players on the allowlist can join (see the Players tab).

online-mode.label: Check accounts (online mode)
online-mode.hint: Checks with Mojang/Microsoft that every player has a real account.
online-mode.caution: When off, anyone can pretend to be anyone, including you. Only turn it off when a proxy (e.g. Velocity) in front checks accounts.

allow-flight.label: Allow flight
allow-flight.hint: Stops players with flight mods or some plugins from being kicked for “flying”.

spawn-protection.label: Spawn protection
spawn-protection.hint: Within this radius (in blocks) around spawn only operators can build. 0 turns it off.

player-idle-timeout.label: Disconnect idle players
player-idle-timeout.hint: Players who don't move for this many minutes are disconnected. 0 = never.

op-permission-level.label: Operator permission level
op-permission-level.hint: 1 = bypass spawn protection, 2 = cheats, 3 = manage players, 4 = everything including stopping the server.

default-player-permission-level.label: Default rights for new players
default-player-permission-level.hint: Which rights players get when they first join.

enforce-secure-profile.label: Require signed chat
enforce-secure-profile.hint: Players need a Mojang-signed profile to chat. Turn off if older clients have trouble.

hide-online-players.label: Hide player list
hide-online-players.hint: Doesn't show who is online in the server list.

level-name.label: World name
level-name.hint: The folder of the active world.

level-seed.label: Seed for new worlds
level-seed.hint: The same seed gives the same world. Only used when a new world is created.

level-type.label: World type
level-type.hint: What new worlds look like. Only used when a new world is created.

generate-structures.label: Generate structures
generate-structures.hint: Villages, temples, strongholds and more in new areas.

allow-nether.label: Allow the Nether
allow-nether.hint: Whether players can travel to the Nether.

spawn-monsters.label: Monsters
spawn-monsters.hint: Whether hostile monsters such as zombies and creepers spawn.

view-distance.label: View distance
view-distance.hint: How many chunks (16 × 16 blocks) players see around them. Less takes a lot of load off the server.

simulation-distance.label: Active area
simulation-distance.hint: Within how many chunks around players crops grow and animals move. Less = less load.

tick-distance.label: Active area
tick-distance.hint: Within how many chunks around players the world runs (4 to 12). Less = less load.

max-world-size.label: Maximum world size
max-world-size.hint: Radius of the world border in blocks. Smaller keeps the world and backups small.

enable-command-block.label: Command blocks
enable-command-block.hint: Allows command blocks for adventure maps and minigames.

resource-pack.label: Resource pack (link)
resource-pack.hint: Direct download link to a ZIP with textures that players get when they join.

require-resource-pack.label: Require resource pack
require-resource-pack.hint: Players who decline the pack can't join.

texturepack-required.label: Require texture pack
texturepack-required.hint: Players must load the server's texture packs.

enable-status.label: Show in the server list
enable-status.hint: Off: the server shows as offline in the list, but people can still join.

sync-chunk-writes.label: Safe saving
sync-chunk-writes.hint: Writes chunks to disk right away. Safer during power cuts, but a bit slower.

network-compression-threshold.label: Compress network from
network-compression-threshold.hint: Packets from this size (bytes) are compressed. -1 turns it off. The default 256 nearly always fits.

max-tick-time.label: Freeze detection
max-tick-time.hint: After this many milliseconds without progress the server considers itself crashed. -1 turns it off.

entity-broadcast-range-percentage.label: View distance for mobs
entity-broadcast-range-percentage.hint: How far animals and monsters are visible, in percent. Less saves bandwidth.

restartHint.plugins: New or changed plugins are only loaded after a restart.
restartHint.mods: New or changed mods are only loaded after a restart.

content.emptyText: Pick something from the marketplace or drag a .jar file here.
content.dropHint: Tip: just drag .jar files onto this page. Switching off renames the file to .jar.disabled.
content.deleteText: The file stays in the trash for 7 days. The plugin's settings folder is kept.

intro.plugins: Plugins extend your server, e.g. with homes, protection or minigames. Find new ones with "Add".
intro.mods: Mods change the game. Players usually need the same mods in their own Minecraft.

sourceNote.modrinth: Modrinth: checked files with a checksum.
sourceNote.hangar: Hangar: PaperMC's plugin marketplace, with a checksum.
sourceNote.spiget: SpigotMC: only free plugins hosted there directly. No checksum.
sourceNote.curseforge: CurseForge: with your own API key.

market.manualTitle: Please install these yourself (external site only):
market.externalHint: This plugin is only offered on an external site. Download it there and drag the .jar into the “Installed” tab.
market.noResultsText: Try another search term or switch off “Only fitting”.
market.keyMissingText: An administrator can enter a free key from console.curseforge.com in the panel settings.
market.notFitWarning: This version is not made for your Minecraft version. It can cause errors or crashes.

backups.started: Backup started. Depending on the world size this can take a few minutes.
backups.emptyText: A backup is a copy of your server with world, plugins and settings. With it you can always go back.
backups.restoreText: The current files are saved as a safety backup first. Then the backup is restored.
backups.restoreTextRunning: The server is stopped for this. The current files are saved as a safety backup first, then the backup is restored and the server starts again.
backups.deleteText: The backup is deleted for good.
backups.settingsText: Older backups are deleted automatically so the disk does not fill up.
backups.excludeHint: Folders with a trailing / (logs/), file types with a star (*.log). You rarely need logs and cache.
backups.title: Backups
backups.intro: Copies of your world and files. One click brings back an earlier state.

schedules.dialogText: What should happen and when? The server then does it on its own.
schedules.monthlyAt: On day {{day}} of every month at {{time}}
schedules.commandHint: A console command without a slash, e.g. say Hello or weather clear.
schedules.ranFailed: “{{name}}” did not work (is the server running?)
schedules.emptyText: Let the server restart at night or back up regularly, no cron needed. Pick a quick template or create your own schedule.
schedules.timezoneNote: Times are in the panel's time zone.
schedules.deleteText: The schedule will no longer run.
schedules.title: Routines
schedules.intro: Create routines to automate tasks on your server: restarts, backups or regular chat messages.

webhooks.title: Notifications
webhooks.subtitle: Messages to Discord, Slack or Teams when a server starts, crashes or a backup is done.
webhooks.dialogText: Choose where messages go and for which events.
webhooks.urlKeep: Leave empty to keep the current address ({{host}}).

howTo.discord: In Discord: Server settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → “Copy webhook URL”.
howTo.slack: In Slack: add the “Incoming Webhooks” app, choose a channel and copy the webhook URL.
howTo.teams: In Teams: channel → Workflows → “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received” and copy the URL.
howTo.generic: An HTTPS address we send JSON to (e.g. for your own scripts or Home Assistant).

webhooks.testFailed: The service rejected the message (error {{status}}). Is the address right?
webhooks.testUnreachable: The service could not be reached.
webhooks.emptyText: Connect Discord, Slack or Teams and know right away when a server crashes.
webhooks.deleteText: No more messages will be sent there.

ddos.title: DDoS protection

headline.failed: Protection could not be switched on
headline.no_host: A part on the computer is still missing

stateText.active: Anyone sending too many connections or packets gets slowed down. Normal players do not notice anything.
stateText.off: Switch it on so single troublemakers cannot knock your servers over.
stateText.waiting: The computer picks up the setting within a few seconds.
stateText.stuck: The helper on the computer has not reported back for a few minutes.
stateText.failed: The firewall rules could not be set. Your servers keep running normally.
stateText.no_host: For safety the panel may not touch the firewall itself. A small helper on the computer does that.

ddos.switchHint: Slows down per sender: too many new connections, too many at once, UDP floods (Bedrock, voice chat) and broken packets. Home network and NetBird stay free.
ddos.installTitle: Set up the helper on the computer
ddos.stuckTitle: Check the helper on the computer
ddos.installText: Enter this once on the computer (or in the Proxmox container) – an update sets it up as well:

error.iptables_missing: iptables is missing on the computer.

ddos.errorHint: Usually a kernel module is missing (xt_hashlimit, xt_connlimit). In a Proxmox container the Proxmox host loads it: run “modprobe -a xt_hashlimit xt_connlimit xt_conntrack xt_comment” there once, then switch off and on again.
ddos.noDocker: Docker was not found yet – the server ports are protected once Docker runs (happens automatically within a minute).
ddos.noSysctl: SYN cookies and the bigger connection table are up to the host here (e.g. Proxmox). The firewall rules work anyway.

limits.tcpNew: At most {{count}} new connections per minute and sender (up to {{burst}} at once) – enough for a whole family behind one connection.
limits.tcpConnections: At most {{count}} open connections at the same time per sender (a player needs one).
limits.udp: At most {{count}} UDP packets per second and sender (a Bedrock player sends about 100, voice chat about 50).
limits.invalid: Broken TCP packets that belong to no connection are dropped; SYN cookies catch SYN floods.
limits.trusted: Never slowed down: your home network, Docker inside and NetBird.

ddos.limitsChange: Put your own limits into this file on the computer:
ddos.honestTitle: What the protection can do – and what not
ddos.honestText: It helps against single troublemakers and small floods: bots connecting thousands of times, or someone flooding your Bedrock port. Against big attacks that clog your whole internet line nothing running at your home helps – the line is full before a packet reaches your computer. Only a service in front of your connection helps there:

tcpshield.name: TCPShield
tcpshield.text: Made for Minecraft Java, free to start. Players connect to TCPShield, which only passes clean connections on to you.

cloudflare.name: Cloudflare Spectrum
cloudflare.text: Protects any TCP/UDP port, Bedrock too. Costs money; for the panel plain Cloudflare (HTTPS) is enough and free.

netbird.name: NetBird proxy on a rented server
netbird.text: If your NetBird runs on a rented server, the world only sees its address. Many providers (e.g. IONOS, Hetzner) filter big attacks there already.

ddos.rateText: Minecraft can kick players who send extremely many packets (for example with cheat tools). A normal game sends far fewer.
ddos.rateHint: Applies to all Java servers from their next start (in server.properties: rate-limit).

account.step2: Scan the QR code or type in the key.

admin.panelDomainHint: Just the name, e.g. panel.myname.com. Passkeys will belong to this address.
admin.domainActive: ✅ You are connected through this domain with HTTPS right now. Passkeys work.

admin.httpsStep2: Put a reverse proxy with HTTPS in front, e.g. Nginx Proxy Manager or Caddy. Target: http://<panel IP>:8080.
admin.httpsStep3: Set MH_TRUST_PROXY=true in the .env and restart the panel (command: update).

passwordReset.cardText: Someone forgot their password? Create a new one and pass it on. All of that person's open sessions end.
passwordReset.title: New password for {{name}}?
passwordReset.text: MorniHosting creates a strong password and shows it to you once. {{name}} is signed out everywhere.

netbird.intro: NetBird gives you HTTPS and your own domain without opening a port on your router. All values below match your panel – just copy them.
netbird.baseHint: The part you enter at NetBird under “Custom Domains”, e.g. mc.your-domain.com. Each service gets its own name in front, like panel.mc.your-domain.com.
netbird.step1Title: Put NetBird on the machine running MorniHosting
netbird.step1Text: Install the NetBird client where MorniHosting runs (e.g. in the Proxmox container) and sign it in with a setup key. You get the key in the NetBird dashboard under “Setup Keys” → “Create Setup Key”.
netbird.step1Lxc: Does MorniHosting run in a Proxmox container (LXC)? With MorniHosting's Proxmox one-liner it is already prepared. If you created the container yourself, NetBird needs a network device there: add these two lines on the Proxmox host to /etc/pve/lxc/<ID>.conf and restart the container:
netbird.step1Router: Does NetBird already run on another device in your home network (as a router)? Then a resource for {{ip}} under Networks is enough – you pick it as the target later.
netbird.step2Add: In the NetBird dashboard: Reverse Proxy → Custom Domains → Add Domain. Enter this domain (without *) and save:
netbird.step2Dns: Then add this record at your domain provider (NetBird shows the exact value after saving):
netbird.step2Verify: Back at NetBird: Verify Domain → Start Verification. Once it says Active, continue. Usually this takes a few minutes, at most 24 hours.
netbird.step3Title: Make the panel reachable over HTTPS
netbird.step3Add: Reverse Proxy → Services → Add Service, then Add Target. As target, pick Peer and your MorniHosting machine – or Host with the IP below if NetBird runs on another device in your home network:
netbird.step3Host: Under Settings, best turn on Pass Host Header. Then the panel sees your domain directly (signing in and passkeys also work without it).
netbird.step3Auth: You can leave Authentication empty, MorniHosting has its own sign-in. If only people in your NetBird should see the panel, choose NetBird-Only Access.
netbird.step3Result: Your panel will then be here:
netbird.step4Text: Create one service for each entry below: mode as given (TCP or UDP), any subdomain, target as in step 3 (peer or host) with the port given. TCP and UDP need no HTTPS and no sign-in.
netbird.noServers: Create a server first, then its ports show up here.
netbird.step4Port: After saving, NetBird shows the port your friends come in on (NetBird Cloud assigns it automatically). Enter it at the server under Settings → Public port, for voice chat in the voice chat box. Then MorniHosting shows the right address everywhere.
netbird.step4Srv: Tip for Java: with an SRV record at your domain provider (_minecraft._tcp.{{name}} → target {{name}}, NetBird's port) friends type just the name, no port.
netbird.step5Text: Open https://{{address}}, sign in and add a passkey under My account. From then on your fingerprint is enough.
netbird.autoHint: Rather not type anything? Connect NetBird once under Server addresses automatically, then MorniHosting sets up every server itself.
netbird.panelNameHint: The part in front of your domain the panel should be reachable at – e.g. hosting for hosting.example.com.

voiceChat.title: Voice chat (Simple Voice Chat)
voiceChat.text: Talk like in real life: players close to each other hear each other. One click installs Simple Voice Chat, opens a UDP port and sets the address for players.
voiceChat.installing: Installing and setting up Simple Voice Chat …
voiceChat.publicPortHint: Only needed when NetBird, playit.gg or your router use a different port to the outside.
voiceChat.playersHint: Every player needs the “Simple Voice Chat” mod in their own Minecraft (Fabric, Forge or NeoForge). Without it they can still play but hear nothing.
voiceChat.routerHint: For friends outside your Wi-Fi, forward UDP port {{port}} on your router – or use NetBird (guide in the admin area).

netbirdAuto.title: Server addresses automatically (NetBird)
netbirdAuto.text: Connect NetBird once and pick your domain. After that you only give each server a name, and MorniHosting creates everything in NetBird itself, e.g. minecraft.your-domain.com.
netbirdAuto.tokenHint: In the NetBird dashboard, create a service user with the “Admin” role under Team → Service Users and choose “Create Token”. The key starts with nbp_ and is stored encrypted.
netbirdAuto.tokenKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored key.
netbirdAuto.apiUrlHint: For NetBird Cloud, keep https://api.netbird.io. If you run NetBird yourself, enter the address of your NetBird dashboard, e.g. https://netbird.your-domain.com. If NetBird is installed on the machine running MorniHosting, the panel picks the address up by itself on the next update.
netbirdAuto.noDomains: Your NetBird has no domain yet. How to add one is explained in the “NetBird” tab above (step 2).
netbirdAuto.domainHint: From “Reverse Proxy → Custom Domains”. Only confirmed domains can be chosen.
netbirdAuto.machineHint: The machine in your NetBird network that MorniHosting runs on. With the Proxmox one-liner it is called “mornihosting”.
netbirdAuto.portNote: NetBird assigns the outside port itself. MorniHosting shows your friends the full address, e.g. minecraft.{{domain}}:31234.
netbirdAuto.disconnectText: MorniHosting deletes the servers' services in NetBird again; the servers no longer have an address through NetBird. The panel's address stays.
netbirdAuto.panelText: Makes the panel reachable under your domain with HTTPS – with “Pass Host Header”, so passkeys work. If the service already exists in NetBird, it is taken over and set up correctly.
netbirdAuto.fieldHint: Just the name – MorniHosting sets up the rest (via NetBird or your own domain). Removing it takes the address away again.
netbirdAuto.createHint: Suggested from the name. Leave empty if the server should not get its own address.
netbirdAuto.portNoteFixed: Your NetBird uses the server's own port outside, e.g. minecraft.{{domain}} for port 25565 – no port number needed.

selfHosted.title: Self-hosted NetBird: open the ports
selfHosted.fixed: The NetBird proxy only lets port 443 through by default. Open these ports once – in your NetBird server's docker-compose.yml under the netbird-proxy service, then run “docker compose up -d”. New servers get the next free port (25566, 25567 …); easiest is to open a range right away, e.g. “25565-25575:25565-25575/tcp”.
selfHosted.random: The NetBird proxy only lets port 443 through by default, and your NetBird assigns its own port per server. Open each of these ports – in your NetBird server's docker-compose.yml under the netbird-proxy service, then run “docker compose up -d”. If your proxy allows custom ports, MorniHosting uses the servers' own ports (25565 …) automatically.
selfHosted.firewall: If your provider has its own firewall in the customer panel (e.g. IONOS, Hetzner), open the same ports there – no script can reach it. By hand works too: add the ports above to netbird-proxy in docker-compose.yml, or run the proxy with “network_mode: host”.
selfHosted.auto: Easiest: run this command once on your NetBird server. It opens 25565–25575/tcp, 19132–19140/udp and 24454–24460/udp on netbird-proxy (and in ufw/firewalld if active) and restarts only the proxy.

netbirdAuto.managedDns: Set up through your own domain.

minecraftAccount.title: Minecraft account
minecraftAccount.text: Link your Minecraft account (Java). Then you see your own head at the bottom left, and on every server you own you are an operator (OP) automatically.
minecraftAccount.name: Your Minecraft name
minecraftAccount.linked: {{name}} is linked – you are now OP on your servers.
minecraftAccount.note: For Java servers. A running server gets it right away, otherwise at the next start. Operators you added yourself stay when you unlink.

dnsAuto.title: Own domain (without NetBird)
dnsAuto.text: If you have your own domain, MorniHosting writes the addresses at your DNS provider itself: every named server becomes name.your-domain.com, and Java players need no port thanks to an SRV record. When your public IP changes, the panel follows within 5 minutes (like DynDNS).
dnsAuto.tokenKeep: Leave empty to keep using the stored key.

tokenHint.cloudflare: dash.cloudflare.com → Profile → API Tokens → “Create Token” → template “Edit zone DNS” → choose your domain as zone. The domain must use Cloudflare's name servers (Cloudflare shows them when you add the domain). Stored encrypted.
tokenHint.ionos: developer.hosting.ionos.de → create an “API key”. It looks like prefix.secret – paste both together with the dot. Stored encrypted.
tokenHint.inwx: The login of your INWX account. Safest is a separate sub-account just for DNS (INWX: “Account → Sub-accounts”). If the account uses two-factor login, enter the secret INWX showed when setting up 2FA (not the 6-digit code). Everything is stored encrypted.

dnsAuto.noZones: This key cannot manage any domain. Check that it is valid for your domain.
dnsAuto.connected: Own domain connected – named servers now get their address.
dnsAuto.summary: Server names become name.{{domain}} at {{provider}} · points to {{ip}} (checked {{time}})
dnsAuto.portNote: The ports still need to be forwarded to this machine in your router (e.g. TCP 25565). You give the name when creating a server or in its settings.
dnsAuto.disconnected: Own domain disconnected – the records are deleted.
dnsAuto.disconnectText: MorniHosting deletes all records it created at your DNS provider. The servers keep running but are only reachable by IP.
dnsAuto.netbirdActive: NetBird hands out the addresses right now. For an own domain without NetBird, disconnect NetBird first (card below).

https.title: HTTPS for the panel
https.text: One click starts a small web server (Caddy) that fetches the certificate by itself. Then https://{{domain}} opens the panel, and every address below it (e.g. survival.{{domain}}) leads there in the browser too. First forward TCP 80 and 443 to this machine in your router.
https.on: HTTPS is running – the certificate arrives on the first visit.

landing.tagline: Your Minecraft server is waiting for you
landing.text: Get started! Java, Bedrock or both together – your server runs within a minute, with its own address under {{domain}}, mods, backups and everything else.
landing.gamesText: Pick what you start with – version and software can be changed any time.

java.title: Minecraft Java Edition
java.text: Paper, Purpur, Fabric, Forge, NeoForge or Vanilla – for PC and Mac.

bedrock.title: Minecraft Bedrock Edition
bedrock.text: For phone, console and Windows – the store edition.

crossplay.title: Minecraft Geyser
crossplay.text: Java server Bedrock players can join too – phone, console and PC together.

mods.title: Mods & plugins in one click
mods.text: Modrinth, CurseForge, Hangar and SpigotMC – only what fits your version, dependencies included.

worlds.title: Upload and download worlds

subdomain.title: Free subdomain
subdomain.text: Give your server a name – friends join via name.{{domain}}.

backups.text: Back up with a click or on a schedule, restarts with a warning in chat.

order.pickText: Pick the edition – then put your server together like at a hoster, just for free.
order.performanceText: Set the slots & power. More memory (RAM) = more players and mods.
order.customText: Need a different size? Set the memory yourself.
order.recommendation: For {{software}} we recommend at least {{ram}}. The player count is a guide – many mods need more.
order.softwareText: The server software decides whether plugins or mods run. Not sure? Paper suits most servers.
order.name: Choose a server name
order.nameText: The address players use to connect to your server.
order.addressReady: Players connect with {{hostname}}. You can change the name any time later.
order.noDomain: No own domain set up yet – players then connect by IP and port. You can set up a domain in the admin area.
order.displayNameHint: The server's name in the panel. Empty = same as the address.
order.addOnsText: Extras for your server. All included and changeable any time.
order.geyserText: Phones, consoles and Windows edition can join.
order.voiceText: Simple Voice Chat: talk to each other in Minecraft, louder the closer you are.
order.backupsText: A backup of your world every day at {{time}}.
order.startNow: Start the server right after ordering
order.changeLater: Power & add-ons can be changed any time
order.bedrockJoin: Bedrock players enter {{hostname}} as server address and {{port}} as port. Bedrock knows no addresses with a built-in port – only a server on 19132 works without entering a port.
order.geyserJoin: Java players just type {{hostname}}. Bedrock players use the same address; the server page shows the port after creating (the first server gets 19132, which is already prefilled).
order.pickPlan: Pick a package – the player count is a guide.
order.pickSoftware: Pick a server software, then the version.
order.pickName: Give your server a name – it becomes its address under {{domain}}. The dice suggests one.

version.title: Minecraft version
version.text: Choose server software and Minecraft version. Your world stays; the server fetches new files on its next start.
version.switchHint: Click a software, pick the version and switch. Plugins and mods of the old software usually stop working – make a backup first.
version.stopFirst: Stop the server to switch the software.
version.addOnsOff: Turn off Bedrock players (Geyser) and voice chat in the Network tab first.
version.saved: {{software}} {{version}} is set. Applies on the next start.

network.title: Network
network.text: Address for your friends, reachability from outside, Bedrock players and voice chat.

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.text: Details for help and support – and deleting the server.

changelog.title: What's new
changelog.running: Your panel runs {{version}}. These are the latest changes:
changelog.updateReady_one: An update is ready – have a look
changelog.failed: GitHub cannot be reached right now. Try again later.

mail.title: Sending e-mail
mail.text: With a mailbox (SMTP) the panel can send mails. Without these settings everything works as before.
mail.hostHint: The address of the outgoing server, e.g. smtp.example.com.
mail.securityHint: “TLS” (port 465) and “STARTTLS” (port 587) are both secure. Not sure? The test below tries both. “None” only inside your own network.
mail.passwordHint: Stored encrypted and never shown again.
mail.passwordKept: A password is saved. Leave empty to keep it.
mail.fromHint: How the mail appears to the recipient, e.g. MorniHosting <noreply@mornihosting.de>.
mail.needsDomain: Links in mails need the panel's domain (tab “Domain & HTTPS”). Until then sign-up and “password forgotten” stay off.
mail.registration: Allow sign-up on the start page
mail.registrationHint: New people create their own account and must confirm their e-mail address with a link. They only get standard rights.
mail.registrationOrdersHint: Without this switch you have to approve new accounts first (Users → “May create servers”).
mail.crashMails: Mail admins when a server crashes
mail.crashMailsHint: At most one mail per server every 15 minutes, in addition to webhooks.
mail.testHint: Leave empty to send it to your own address (My account).
mail.helpTitle: Where do I get a mail server?
mail.helpInwx: INWX: create a mailbox for noreply@your-domain in the customer menu. Server and port are in the mailbox details (usually mail.inwx.de, port 587).
mail.helpIonos: IONOS: create a mailbox. Server smtp.ionos.com, port 587, the user is the full address.
mail.helpGmail: Gmail: smtp.gmail.com, port 587. You need an “app password” (Google account → Security → 2-step verification → App passwords), not your normal password.
mail.internalHostHint: Optional. If the mail server is in your home network, enter its IP here (e.g. 192.168.178.116). The panel then connects to this IP but still checks the certificate against the name above.
mail.switched: Port {{old}} did not answer, port {{port}} with {{security}} did. That is saved now.

unreachable.title: Mail server not found
unreachable.tip: The name cannot be resolved or the machine does not answer. If the mail server is in your home network, enter its IP under “Internal server address (IP)”. An /etc/hosts entry does not help because the panel runs in its own container.

port_closed.title: Port closed
port_closed.tip: The mail server is reachable but accepts nothing on port {{port}}. Check which ports it listens on (Stalwart: usually 465 with TLS) and whether a firewall is in the way.

timeout.title: No answer (after 10 seconds)
timeout.tip: Nothing came back on port {{port}}. Often the name points to another machine from outside (e.g. NetBird) or a firewall drops the connection. Enter the mail server’s internal IP and try port 465 with TLS.

wrong_security.title: Encryption does not match the port
wrong_security.tip: Port 465 needs “TLS”, port 587 needs “STARTTLS”. Set the encryption to match the port.

tls.title: Certificate does not match
tls.tip: No secure connection: the certificate does not match the name, has expired or is self-signed. Enter exactly the name from the certificate under “Mail server” (e.g. mail.pmornhart.de) and put the IP only in the “internal” field. The check stays on for security.

login.title: Login refused
login.tip: User or password is wrong. With Stalwart the user is usually the full address, e.g. noreply@mornihosting.de. Enter the password again, save and test once more.

sender.title: Sender refused
sender.tip: The mail server does not allow this account to send as {{from}}. Use the account’s own address as sender or allow it for this account on the mail server.

recipient.title: Recipient refused
recipient.tip: The mail server does not accept this recipient. Check the spelling or try another address.

other.title: Unexpected error
other.tip: This matches no known cause. The reply below helps to look further.

mailPages.usernameHint: Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore.
mailPages.registerText: Your own Minecraft server in a few clicks. First we need your e-mail address.
mailPages.registerSent: We sent a mail to {{email}}. Click the link in it, then you can log in. Nothing there? Check your spam folder too.
mailPages.forgotText: Enter your e-mail address. We will send you a link to choose a new password.
mailPages.forgotSent: If an account exists for this address, a mail is on its way. The link is valid for one hour.
mailPages.resetText: Choose a new password for your account.
mailPages.resetDone: You can now log in with the new password. All other devices were logged out.

register.title: E-mail confirmed

email_change.title: Address confirmed
email_change.text: Your new e-mail address is saved.

emailCard.title: E-mail address
emailCard.text: For “password forgotten” and order confirmations. A new address only becomes active once you click the link in the mail.
emailCard.label: E-mail address
emailCard.passwordHint: We ask once more, for safety.
emailCard.sent: We sent a mail to {{email}}. Click the link in it.
emailCard.unavailable: E-mail is not set up in this panel yet. Please ask whoever runs it.

games.performanceText: How much memory (RAM) your server gets. More RAM = bigger worlds and more players.
games.versionText: Which version of the server should run. You can change it later in the settings.

versions.latestText: The very newest version – may still have bugs.
versions.steamText: The server fetches the newest version from Steam on every start.
versions.officialText: The server fetches its files with the official Hytale downloader.

games.settingsText: Everything here is optional. You can also fill it in later in the server's settings.
games.settingsCardText: Settings {{game}} itself needs. Passwords and keys are stored encrypted and never shown again.
games.downloadNote: On its first start the server downloads about {{gb}} GB. That can take a few minutes.
games.terms: I follow the terms of use of {{game}}.
games.secretStored: stored – type a new one to change it
games.saved: Saved. Applies from the next start.
games.restartHint: Changes apply from the server's next restart.

factorio.text: Build huge factories together – with belts, trains and Space Age.
factorio.about: Your own Factorio server: it keeps running while you are offline and saves the map automatically.
factorio.memoryHint: {{gb}} GB is enough for most factories. Huge megabases or many mods need more.

fields.usernameHint: Only needed if the panel should update mods automatically.
fields.tokenHint: A key from your Factorio account (not your password). It stays encrypted.
fields.updateModsHint: Downloads new versions of your mods before every start. Needs username and token.
fields.spaceAgeHint: The Space Age expansion (with quality and elevated rails). Every player then needs it too.

cs2.text: Your own Counter-Strike 2 server – competitive, deathmatch or workshop maps.
cs2.about: Your own Counter-Strike 2 server. Without a Steam token (GSLT) only friends with the address can join; with one it also shows up in the server list.
cs2.memoryHint: {{gb}} GB is enough for 5 versus 5. Take more for community servers with many players.

fields.serverNameHint: What the server is called in the server list.
fields.passwordHint: Anyone who wants to join needs this password. Empty = everyone with the address.
fields.gameModeHint: How you play. Can be changed any time later.
fields.startMapHint: The map after starting, e.g. de_inferno, de_mirage or de_dust2.
fields.maxPlayersHint: How many may play at once (default 10).
fields.gsltHint: A “Game Server Login Token” from Steam, with app id 730. Only needed for the server to show up publicly in the list.
fields.workshopCollectionHint: The number of a Steam Workshop collection with maps (from the collection's address, after “id=”).

gmod.text: Build, mess around or play Trouble in Terrorist Town – with addons from the workshop.
gmod.about: Your own Garry's Mod server. Addons and maps come easiest through a Steam Workshop collection.
gmod.memoryHint: {{gb}} GB is enough for most servers. Many addons need more.

fields.serverNameHint: What the server is called in the server list.
fields.gamemodeHint: e.g. sandbox or terrortown (TTT). Other modes come through the workshop collection.
fields.workshopCollectionHint: The number of your Steam Workshop collection (from its address, after “id=”). The server downloads all addons from it.
fields.authKeyHint: The server needs it to download the workshop collection. Stays encrypted.
fields.mapHint: The map after starting, e.g. gm_construct or gm_flatgrass.
fields.maxPlayersHint: How many may play at once (default 16).
fields.passwordHint: No spaces. Empty = everyone with the address can join.
fields.gsltHint: A “Game Server Login Token” with app id 4000. Only needed for the server to stay in the list.

games.noConsole: This game has no console for the panel. You manage the server in the game itself.

satisfactory.text: Build a huge factory together on an alien planet – up to 8 players.
satisfactory.about: Your own Satisfactory server. After the first start, add it in the game under “Server Manager” with its address and set its name and admin password there. If the computer runs on Proxmox, set the VM's CPU type to “host” – otherwise the server will not start.
satisfactory.memoryHint: Satisfactory needs a lot of memory: {{gb}} GB is a good start, big factories need 16 GB.

fields.maxPlayersHint: How many may play at once (default 4, officially up to 8).
fields.autosavesHint: How many automatic saves are kept.
fields.experimentalHint: Downloads the Experimental branch from Steam. All players then need Experimental too.

files.done: Everything is there – the server can start.

ets2.text: Drive together in a convoy across Europe – on your own server, even while you are offline.
ets2.about: Your own convoy server for Euro Truck Simulator 2 (up to 8 drivers). Before the first start you need two files only the game itself can make – the panel shows you how.
ets2.memoryHint: {{gb}} GB is enough for a convoy of 8 drivers.
ets2.filesText: The server needs your map and DLC list from the game. This is how you get the two files:
filesSteps: Start Euro Truck Simulator 2 and load your profile.
Open config.cfg in “Documents/Euro Truck Simulator 2” and set uset g_console to "1".
In the game press the ~ key, type export_server_packages and press Enter.
“Documents/Euro Truck Simulator 2” now holds server_packages.sii and server_packages.dat – upload both here.

fields.lobbyNameHint: What the server is called in the convoy list in game.
fields.passwordHint: Anyone who wants to drive along needs this password. Empty = everyone.
fields.maxPlayersHint: How many may drive at once (at most 8).
fields.welcomeHint: Shows in the chat when someone joins.
fields.logonTokenHint: Optional: a “Game Server Login Token” with app id 227300. It keeps the server's id the same.

hytale.text: Explore, build and fight together in the world of Hytale.
hytale.about: Your own Hytale server. On the first start a link shows up in the console: open it and sign in with your Hytale account so the server may download the official files. Then type /auth login device into the console and sign the server in the same way.
hytale.memoryHint: {{gb}} GB is a good start. Big worlds or many players need more.

fields.autoUpdateHint: Downloads the newest server version before every start. Off = only on the first start.
